Rationale: contract.declared_missing is non-empty - `attachments` is declared as a response array and came back entirely absent, not even as []. A declared-but-absent field is DRIFT by definition ('invoked, but declared and actual disagree'), not PASS ('the response carries what the contract declares'). Precedent in this suite: edit_project_v1 (access_type/user_role/permissions), get_test_plan_v2 (parent_plan_id), list_test_runs_v2 (issues/issue_tracker) and get_test_plan_test_runs_v2 (test_runs[].test_plan) were all DRIFT on exactly this basis. Labelling this PASS would make the batches non-comparable.
Severity is genuinely low - the subagent's reading that it is 'omitted when empty, and undocumented as such' is plausible - but it still has a concrete consequence: an agent that does attachments.length or iterates it gets a TypeError rather than an empty loop, because the key is missing rather than empty.
What is NOT in doubt, and is the headline result: this capability does NOT reproduce the create_root_folder_v1 twin defect. The declared flat body worked on the first real attempt, its json_path (/test_case/<field>) is internal wire-mapping metadata that its guidance correctly never asks the caller to replicate, its flat returns array and nested schema AGREE (unusual in this batch), urls came back as a properly-declared {self} object rather than an under-declared bare object, and no undeclared fields were returned.
